policy: Update deliberately ONLY when a model change intentionally moves the baseline. Never edit to hide a regression.

history.reason: Superseded. Warning thresholds were hand-picked per signal in raw units — 3.0 psi for unit_n_delta_p, 0.5 % for salt_passage — which on this dataset is 6.6 sigma versus 12.2 sigma of each signal's own clean-window spread. Ranking the two by (precision+recall)/2 while holding one to a nearly twice stricter bar measured which threshold was kinder, not which signal leads. Thresholds are now WARN_SIGMA robust sigmas of each signal's own spread. WARN_SIGMA = 4.0 matches deviation.py's existing OUT_OF_RANGE_Z rather than being tuned against this backtest, and validation_report.json now publishes the full 4-12 sigma sweep. salt_passage ranks first at every sigma except 12.2, so the leading-indicator finding does not depend on the choice. Effect on the leading indicator: recall 0.211 -> 0.380, median lead 39 -> 53 days, true positives 15 -> 27, precision 0.500 -> 0.474.
